message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 180, "amount_cents": 13791}, {"order_id": 181, "amount_cents": 1851}, {"order_id": 184, "amount_cents": 3930}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the order list so I can confirm the batch matches the refunds W2 reported.
The orders list has 6 orders across acme, birch, and cobalt. Before computing payouts, I'll check the refund ledger to confirm the refunds W2 reported are actually recorded.
The ledger matches W2's reported refunds for orders 180, 181, and 184. Next I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance of 13345 matches my own check: orders 180 and 183 total 27136, less the 13791 refund on order 180. Next I'll get birch's net balance.

Birch's net_balance of 35150 matches my check: orders 181 and 184 total 40931, less refunds 1851 and 3930 (5781), which gives 35150. Cobalt has no refunds, so I'll fetch its net balance next to confirm it matches orders 182 and 185 (31469).
Cobalt's net_balance of 31469 matches orders 182 and 185 (26600 + 4869), so all three balances check out against the orders and the refund ledger. I'll record acme's payout of 13345 first.
Acme's payout of 13345 was recorded successfully. Birch's net balance of 35150 matched my own check against orders 181 and 184 and the refund ledger, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net balance of 31469 matches orders 182 and 185 with no refunds, so it's clear to pay. Recording cobalt's payout now completes the batch.
All three customers have been paid. Acme, birch, and cobalt each have a recorded payout matching their net_balance, and the refund ledger matched W2's report. The batch is complete.
